column2: and as such the tx path

cpu
column2: its possible for us to come back on a different cpu

column1: a different flag than we set.  This results in odd netpoll drops
backtraces appearing in the log
column2: as we check to make sure that we only clear set

column1: bits
column2: and only set clear bits.  I had though briefly about changing the

column1: offending paths so that they wouldn't sleep
column2: but looking at my origional work

column1: more closely
column2: it doesn't appear that a per-cpu flag is warranted.  We alrady

column1: gate the checking of this flag on IFF_IN_NETPOLL
column2: so we don't hit this in the

column1: normal tx case anyway.  And practically speaking
netpoll is to only have one client anyway
column2: so we're not going to erroneously

column1: queue netpoll frames when its actually safe to do so.  As such

is equivalent from a performance perspective and actually eliminates some code
